questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
She is more taller than her sister.
questions.explanation:
Error: Double comparative — 'more' + 'taller' is incorrect.
Rule: Use EITHER 'more' OR the '-er' suffix, never both.
Correct: 'She is taller than her sister.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
The news are very shocking today.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'news' is an uncountable noun (always singular) — it takes a singular verb.
Rule: 'news' → singular verb (is/was), not plural.
Correct: 'The news is very shocking today.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
He run very fast in yesterday's race.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'run' is present tense but 'yesterday' indicates past tense.
Rule: Past simple is required with time expressions like 'yesterday'.
Correct: 'He ran very fast in yesterday's race.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
I am working here since 2015.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'since + specific year' requires Present Perfect Continuous, not Simple Present.
Rule: 'since' with a point in time → have/has + been + V-ing.
Correct: 'I have been working here since 2015.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
Neither of the boys have completed their homework.
options: neither of the boys has completed his
neither of the boys had completed their
none of the boys have completed their
questions.explanation:
Error: 'neither' is singular — it takes a singular verb and singular pronoun.
Rule: neither/either/each/one + of + plural noun → singular verb.
Correct: 'Neither of the boys has completed his homework.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
She saw him to cross the road carefully.
questions.explanation:
Error: Verbs of perception (see, hear, watch) take object + bare infinitive (without 'to').
Rule: see/hear/watch + object + bare infinitive.
Correct: 'She saw him cross the road carefully.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
He is one of the best student in the college.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'one of the + noun' requires the noun to be plural.
Rule: 'one of the + plural noun' (the verb may still be singular in the main clause).
Correct: 'He is one of the best students in the college.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
She told me that she will come the next day.
questions.explanation:
Error: Reported speech tense shift — 'told' is past, so 'will' must shift to 'would'.
Rule: Direct: will → Indirect (after past reporting verb): would.
Correct: 'She told me that she would come the next day.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
The judge insisted that the witness goes on oath.
questions.explanation:
Error: After verbs of demand/order/insist/suggest, the subjunctive requires the base form of the verb (no -s/-es).
Rule: insist/demand/suggest/recommend + that + subject + bare infinitive.
Correct: 'The judge insisted that the witness go on oath.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
I prefer coffee than tea in the morning.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'.
Rule: prefer A to B (NOT prefer A than B).
Correct: 'I prefer coffee to tea in the morning.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
Being tired, the sofa attracted him.
options: he was attracted to the sofa
questions.explanation:
Error: Dangling modifier — 'Being tired' must refer to the subject of the main clause. The sofa cannot be tired.
Rule: The participial phrase must logically modify the subject that follows.
Correct: 'Being tired, he was attracted to the sofa.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
The number of accidents in the city are increasing.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'The number of' is a singular subject.
Rule: 'The number of + plural noun' → singular verb.
(Contrast: 'A number of students are...' → plural.)
Correct: 'The number of accidents in the city is increasing.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
He congratulated me for winning the competition.
questions.explanation:
Error: Wrong preposition after 'congratulate'.
Rule: congratulate + object + on + V-ing (not 'for').
Correct: 'He congratulated me on winning the competition.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
She is looking forward to meet you next week.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'look forward to' — here 'to' is a PREPOSITION, not part of an infinitive.
Rule: preposition + gerund (V-ing), not bare/to-infinitive.
Correct: 'She is looking forward to meeting you next week.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
He is too intelligent to not understand this problem.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'too…to' already expresses a negative consequence — adding 'not' creates a double negative and reverses the meaning.
Rule: too + adjective + to + bare infinitive (the negative is implied).
Correct: 'He is too intelligent to understand this problem.' means he is SO intelligent he finds it beneath him.
Note: If the intended meaning is 'he cannot understand it', use 'not intelligent enough to understand'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
No sooner did he arrived than it started raining.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'No sooner…than' requires Past Perfect with inversion in the first clause.
Rule: No sooner + had + subject + V3 + than + Past Simple.
Correct: 'No sooner had he arrived than it started raining.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
My father insisted me to come home early.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'insist' cannot take a direct object + to-infinitive construction.
Rule: insist + that + subject + bare infinitive (subjunctive), or insist on + V-ing.
Correct: 'My father insisted that I come home early.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
Between you and I, I think he is dishonest.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'between' is a preposition and must be followed by an object pronoun.
Rule: Use object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them) after prepositions, not subject pronouns (I, he, she, we).
Correct: 'Between you and me, I think he is dishonest.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
The furniture were badly damaged in the flood.
options: The furniture was being badly damaged
questions.explanation:
Error: 'furniture' is an uncountable noun — it has no plural form and always takes a singular verb.
Rule: Uncountable nouns (furniture, luggage, equipment, information) → singular verb.
Correct: 'The furniture was badly damaged in the flood.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
Rita is more intelligent than any student in her class.
questions.explanation:
Error: Rita is herself a student — 'any student' includes Rita, making the comparison illogical.
Rule: When comparing a member to others in its own group, use 'any other'.
Correct: 'Rita is more intelligent than any other student in her class.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
He is used to work late into the night.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'be used to' means 'be accustomed to' — 'to' here is a PREPOSITION, so it must be followed by a gerund (V-ing).
Rule: be/get used to + V-ing (NOT bare infinitive).
Contrast: 'used to + bare infinitive' expresses a past habit (he used to work late = he did so in the past but not now).
Correct: 'He is used to working late into the night.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
Scarcely had she left the office than the fire broke out.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'Scarcely…when' is the correct correlative pair — 'than' is wrong here.
Rule: Scarcely/Hardly + had + subject + V3 + WHEN + past simple.
(No sooner uses 'than'; Scarcely/Hardly use 'when'.)
Correct: 'Scarcely had she left the office when the fire broke out.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
She could not help but to cry when she heard the news.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'help but + to-infinitive' is incorrect — 'cannot help but' takes a BARE infinitive.
Rule: cannot help but + bare infinitive. Alternatively: cannot help + V-ing.
Both 'could not help crying' (option A) and 'could not help but cry' (option C) are correct grammatically, but option C preserves the 'but' construction from the original stem.
Correct: 'She could not help but cry when she heard the news.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
The man who I met at the conference is a renowned scientist.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'who' is a subject pronoun. Here the relative pronoun is the OBJECT of 'met', so the object form 'whom' is required.
Rule: When the relative pronoun is the object of the clause's verb, use 'whom' (not 'who').
Test: I met him (not 'I met he') → object → 'whom'.
Correct: 'The man whom I met at the conference is a renowned scientist.'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem:
Choose the option that best replaces the underlined part, or select 'No improvement'.
He has been living in this city since five years.
questions.explanation:
Error: 'since' is used with a POINT in time (since 2020, since Monday). 'Five years' is a DURATION, not a point in time.
Rule: Use 'for' with duration (for five years, for two months); use 'since' with a specific moment.
Correct: 'He has been living in this city for the last five years.'
questions.subject: English
